subject: Next steps: lane sizing & $/1M token target for StrataSecure
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@stratasecure.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-29T15:22:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap: throughput & pricing inputs we need

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can produce a concise dedicated-lane proposal for StrataSecure: 

- Workloads: you mentioned a mix of short chat-style prompts (~40 tokens avg) and longer completion jobs (900–1,500 tokens) for nightly batch runs.
- Primary goals: keep 99th pct latency < 250ms for interactive, hit predictable monthly cost target.
- Questions / asks for proposal (please confirm):
  1) Expected total monthly tokens (range): best guess low/likely/high (e.g., 50M / 250M / 1B).
  2) Target $/1M tokens you want to negotiate toward (you said ~$35–$50 as an internal threshold on the call?).
  3) Preferred GPU families on reserved capacity (A100-40GB, H100, or open to mixed pools).
  4) Any compliance or private deployment constraints (VPC/on-prem).

We also took a short sample of your trace earlier — if you can share the CSV snapshot you mentioned (token distribution and p95 lengths) that would help us size throughput lanes and batching profiles.

Plan from our side once we have those inputs: 1) two-scenario proposal (pilot: small reserved lane + burst host; scale: 2–4 reserved lanes by workload), 2) per-GPU $/1M token economics, and 3) an optional 90-day pilot credit to validate latency.

Attachments: reference checklist and an empty draft MSA we usually use (will attach once internal review done).

Thanks — I can turn the proposal around by EOD Tuesday once we have numbers.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@stratasecure.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratasecure.com
Date: 2027-05-29T18:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & pricing inputs we need

Marcus — thanks for the summary. Quick answers below and I attached a small CSV with sample token distributions.

1) Monthly tokens (estimated): low 80M, expected 300M, high 1.2B. We anticipate steady ramp over next 6 months if pilot looks good.
2) Target $/1M tokens: internally we'd like to land at ~$30–$40 / 1M tokens for the production lane; pilot can be higher.
3) GPUs: performance is important; our infra team prefers H100 for the production lane if costs can be justified. For pilot we're OK with A100-40GB. Open to mixed pools if you can show unit economics.
4) Compliance: VPC with audit logging; SOC 2 evidence will be required during procurement.

Attachments: inference-workload-snapshot.csv (token buckets, p50/p90/p99 lengths). Procurement is cc'd — they will want a minimal list of required security docs and a redline-friendly MSA.

Would appreciate a proposal that shows: pilot lane (A100) cost, production lane (H100) cost, and a mixed-reserve option along with $/1M token breakouts.

Best,
Emily Hart
Head of ML Ops, StrataSecure
emily.hart@stratasecure.com

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T02:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: throughput & pricing inputs we need

Looping in a quick internal checklist / guidance for the proposal — forwarding Emily's note below. Short bullets for the deliverable: 

- Provide three priced options: Pilot (1 reserved lane, A100), Prod-H100 (2 reserved lanes, H100), Hybrid (1 H100 reserved + 1 A100 reserve + burst pool).
- Show unit economics as $/1M tokens and per-token marginal cost at target throughput. Include both estimated and conservative unit costs.
- Include SLA targets we can realistically hit (p99 latency) and fallback behavior (burst to hosted fleet).
- Offer a 60–90 day pilot credit: recommend 25% credit on pilot bill to remove friction.
- Attach a short appendix mapping token buckets to expected GPU utilization and quota sizing (use Emily CSV).

Also add a line for procurement: list SOC2, ICC (if requested), encryption at rest (KMS) — we'll attach SOC2 report and the draft MSA in the outgoing.

Can you draft the options and send to Emily with links to the HubSpot deal and a DocuSign stub? I'll review before you send.

Thanks — L.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@stratasecure.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, procurement@stratasecure.com
Date: 2027-05-30T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Next steps: lane sizing & $/1M token target for StrataSecure

Emily — thanks for the fast follow. Attached are the three options per Lauren's note and a short appendix that maps your CSV to expected GPU utilization. High level: 

- Pilot (A100-40GB): 1 reserved lane sized for ~300M tokens/month nominal, estimated unit price $52 / 1M tokens; with proposed 25% pilot credit effective $39 / 1M for pilot term.
- Production (H100): 2 reserved lanes sized for 300–1,200M tokens ramp path, estimated unit price $30 / 1M at steady state (after utilization and batching benefits).
- Hybrid: 1 H100 reserved + 1 A100 reserved + burst hosts — blended $/1M ~ $35 (midpoint).

Notes on assumptions: batching efficiencies assume 60–70% of interactive tokens eligible for batching; nightly batch windows assumed to be on separate lane. Pricing includes inference compute only (excludes storage & network). SOC 2 and audit docs attached; Draft MSA attached for procurement redlines.

Next steps: Can we schedule a 45-minute ops deep-dive next week (I propose Tue 6/6 or Wed 6/7) to validate latency SLOs and confirm procurement items? If procurement is ready, we'll load the draft MSA to DocuSign for an initial review round.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/7832 | DocuSign proposal: https://www.docusign.com/link/proposal-DEAL-7832

Attachments: StrataSecure_MLSpecs.pdf, Draft-MSA-StrataSecure.docx

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—Marcus
